subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting arbitrary configured workspace files changes deterministic system-prompt context loading and the public hook behavior.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename workspace files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement preserves path guards, budgets, docs, diagnostics, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep custom context in first-class workspace filenames, plugin hooks, or on-demand file reads.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Leave this open until a broader context/config API covers custom startup files without adding another point contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename workspace files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement preserves path guards, budgets, docs, diagnostics, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and authored adjacent boundary-read work, making him the best available owner for the hook contract decision.
